nc_moore_s_wall_routes.blurb: Moore's Wall sits in Hanging Rock State Park, in the Sauratown Mountains of North Carolina's Piedmont, close to Danbury. The rock is rugged, sharp quartzite with ledges, overhangs and technical top-outs, and the holds lean toward slopers and crimps. Trad is by far the main event, backed by a small number of bolted lines. Grades run from 5.5 up to 5.14, with the bulk between 5.10 and 5.12 and a modest set of moderates below. Protection can be in less obvious spots, so careful route reading matters. North End, Hanging Garden, the Amphitheater and Central Wall are the busiest walls. Fall is the favored season, and summer heat and humidity are best avoided.

co_east_animas.blurb: East Animas is a sandstone crag on the east side of the Animas Valley, just outside Durango and visible from the road north out of town. It faces west, so mornings are shady and afternoons sunny. Spring and fall are usually best, with summer comfortable in the shade and winter pleasant in the sun. Trad makes up the larger share, with a solid block of sport routes alongside, mostly one or two pitches long. Grades start easy but gather between 5.9 and 5.12, with a handful of 5.13 and 5.14 lines for strong climbers. Watch Crystal, Apple Cider, Jabba Buttress and Bedrock are the biggest walls. Expect some loose rock and grades that can feel stiff.

co_penitente_canyon.blurb: Penitente Canyon is a canyon of low cliffs and buttresses in the San Luis Valley of south-central Colorado, surrounded by pinon and juniper. The walls are volcanic tuff, and routes are short, often 25 to 75 feet. Sport climbing dominates by a wide margin, with technical, crimpy lines mostly between 5.10 and 5.12 plus a fair set of 5.8 and 5.9 options and a few harder lines above. A smaller number of trad crack lines and a little bouldering fill out the rest. May and October are the prime months, and south-facing routes stay climbable through the year. The Inner Canyon holds the most climbs, with the Entrance Area close behind.

mi_wetmore_landing.blurb: Wetmore Landing is a bouldering zone on Michigan's Upper Peninsula, north of Marquette, and every climb here is a boulder problem. At Rum Runner's Cove the boulders are weathered and sculpted, roughly 15 to 20 feet tall, and face south over Lake Superior. Problems there are crackless and reward balance and careful footwork more than power, and landings can be uneven, so extra pads and spotters help. Grades span the full range but pile up in the easy and moderate bands, from very easy to V3, with a thin tail of hard problems above. Rum Runner's Cove, Freeman Landing, Beach Side and The Point are the main clusters.

ca_green_valley_lake_area.blurb: Green Valley Lake Area lies in the San Bernardino Mountains near Running Springs, at roughly 7,200 feet. Most of the climbing is on Crafts Peak, where short trad formations, pinnacles and big blocks stand on a steep forested ridge with views toward Lake Arrowhead and the San Gabriel Mountains. Routes are mostly short, 20 to 40 feet, with a few formations reaching around 80. Trad dominates, with some sport lines, top-ropes and scattered boulders. Grades run from beginner level up to 5.11, with the heart of it around 5.7 to 5.10. Rock quality swings from smooth and polished to grainy and lichen-covered, sometimes on different sides of one formation. Crafts Peak West, Green Valley Lake Pinnacles and Crab Valley round it out.

qc_07_outaouais.blurb: Outaouais is the Quebec climbing region just north of Ottawa, and most of its popular climbing is concentrated in Gatineau Park, which includes the Eardley Escarpment. Further afield are Rocher du Capitaine, Parc régional de la Forêt Bowman, Rivière Dumoine and Lac en Coeur. Sport and trad share the load almost evenly, with a scattering of boulder problems, top-ropes and one ice line. Grades start gentle but cluster between 5.8 and 5.12, with a few 5.13 lines for stronger climbers. The climbing is divided among many separate sites rather than one big cliff, so it rewards choosing a destination by style and grade before you head out.
